paper_metadata.title: Monte-Carlo Option Pricing in Quantum Parallel

experiments.description: Proposed Monte-Carlo option pricing in quantum parallel (MCQP) for a single-asset Black-Scholes-Merton European call option, with a conceptual quantum circuit and classical simulation studies of pricing error versus number of simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

algorithm.variant: Monte-Carlo Option Pricing in Quantum Parallel (MCQP) with amplitude estimation post-processing
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical simulations use fixed BSM parameters; quantum proposal initializes index register in uniform superposition and uses seed-based stochastic sampling for ΔW.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Index register of size n = log(N) qubits encodes N paths; stochastic variable register of size kv qubits encodes ΔW; stock price register of size ks qubits encodes St; payoff register of size kp qubits encodes payoff P; one ancilla qubit encodes mean payoff amplitude.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate European call option value E[max(ST - K, 0)] discounted by the risk-free rate.

problem_instance.description: Single-asset European call option under Black-Scholes-Merton dynamics; evaluation includes varying strike price and volatility, plus scalability studies over simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic BSM/GBM simulation with initial stock price 100.0, drift 0.05, volatility 0.4, total time 1.0; strike price varied in experiments; price bins discretized into 2^5 bins for the 'Bins' baseline-like comparison; 10,000 Monte Carlo paths for Array MC comparison.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Stock prices discretized into equal-width bins for the 'Bins' comparison; parameter values rounded to nearest of 2^k values in the precision-bit study; ΔW sampled via seed-based rejection sampling in the proposed MCQP construction.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Classical simulations compared against analytical BSM call price; 30 independent trials for the parameter-sweep study; error and standard deviation reported versus number of simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: n + kv + ks + kp + 1, with n = log(N); additional log(m) qubits mentioned for random-number generation input; example index register size approximately 13 qubits for N ≈ 10^4

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical Monte Carlo and analytical BSM pricing used as references; synthetic path generation with Euler-style time stepping; rounding of values to emulate finite qubit precision in the accuracy study.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Mean payoff estimation, discounting by risk-free rate, and error comparison against theoretical BSM price; log-log scaling analysis of error versus simulations/time steps/precision bits.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported standard deviation across 30 trials for parameter sweeps

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming efficient state preparation and use of quantum amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims O(1/N) sampling error for QAE versus O(1/sqrt(N)) classically, but the MCQP state-preparation step is conceptual and not hardware-demonstrated.

speedup_claims.factor: linear qubit overhead in number of dimensions
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity claim, not an empirical speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(m) circuit depth; linear qubit overhead in number of dimensions and precision registers; claimed quadratic speedup in sampling error via amplitude estimation (O(1/M) versus classical O(1/sqrt(N))).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo sampling error O(1/sqrt(N)); arbitrary state preparation noted as exponential in number of qubits in related literature.

experiments.description: Classical simulation study of the proposed random-number seed generation and rejection-sampling routines used to support the MCQP construction, including visual inspection of generated samples.

algorithm.variant: Seed generation via logistic map and rejection sampling for ΔW sampling
algorithm.parameter_initialization: x0 = 1/sqrt(i^3); iterative logistic map x <- 4x(1-x); seed y derived from x and m.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Not a full pricing circuit; generates classical samples intended to populate the stochastic-variable register in the proposed quantum algorithm.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate approximately normally distributed random samples for ΔW using seed-based rejection sampling.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Rejection sampling with acceptance probability based on normalized normal PDF value.

problem_instance.description: Random sample generation for 1000 index values and 100 time-step values to test the seed and rejection-sampling procedures.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic sampling study over i and m indices; no market dataset.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Seed computed from logistic map and time-step index; samples drawn uniformly from [-4.5, 4.5] and accepted/rejected according to normalized normal density.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Visual inspection of output distributions shown in Figures 2 and 3; no quantitative statistical test reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Logistic-map seed generation and rejection sampling.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Visual inspection of generated sample distributions.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a classical support routine study, not a quantum speedup result.

experiments.description: Classical accuracy study emulating the effect of finite quantum precision by rounding parameters, stock prices, and payoffs to a fixed number of precision bits while pricing a BSM European call option.

algorithm.variant: Precision-bit emulation of MCQP pricing accuracy
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Same BSM parameters as the main pricing study; values rounded to nearest of 2^k equally spaced values between bounds.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Finite-precision discretization of parameters, stock prices, and payoffs to emulate qubit-limited registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate BSM European call price under discretized arithmetic.

problem_instance.description: Single-asset European call option under BSM with fixed initial parameters and sweeps over number of simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic BSM simulation; no external dataset.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Numeric values rounded to nearest discretization grid determined by precision bits; stock price bounds assumed [0, 300].
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 30 independent trials; mean error and standard deviation versus theoretical BSM price; log-log plots of error versus simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Rounding of parameters and intermediate products to emulate finite register precision.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison to theoretical BSM price; analysis of mean error and standard deviation.

experiments.description: Conceptual extension of MCQP to nested Monte-Carlo risk analysis for portfolio value-at-risk / threshold-crossing estimation at an intermediate time τ, including a secondary index register and nested path structure.

algorithm.variant: Nested MCQP for single-split risk analysis
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not specified; nested path construction is described symbolically.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Primary index register |i⟩_n and secondary index register |j⟩_n represent N^2 paths from time τ onward; payoff and risk metric are encoded via QDAC/QADC-style amplitude mappings.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate P(Portfolio Value < ε) at time τ, or equivalently a threshold-crossing / VaR-like risk metric.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Thresholding via risk metric function RF applied after nested payoff estimation.

dataset_specification.description: No dataset; symbolic nested simulation setup for a single option and then generalized to portfolios.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No explicit preprocessing; nested simulation uses simulated paths from S0 to τ and from τ to T.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: No numerical results reported; only a proposed circuit/state transformation and qualitative discussion.
